title: Optimal Advertiser-to-Rank Allocation in Parallel Experiments with Shared Unknown Position Discounts
banked_reason: D0.5 cold referee paper-score ceiling 6.4 is below the 7.4 field floor; the remaining quadratic-term objection was independently reproduced as a double-counted summand and operator-adjudicated unsustained.
gap_reasons: D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.4 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'incremental'.
The delivered contribution is an oracle local-information design theory for fixed known lift and discount parameters, not a finite-sample risk result or a feasible pilot-adaptive inference procedure.

The exact higher-dimensional structure covers two crossing symmetry classes—common lower-rank discounts or one-outlier lift magnitude—while the generic case with heterogeneous lifts and discounts remains unclassified.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived the rank-specific Schur geometry, assignment certificate, balanced-allocation converse, two-advertiser solution, and two complementary symmetry reductions. A bounded convexity gap in the assignment certificate was repaired and independently checked. The result remained below the field novelty floor: inference is still oracle-only and the fully heterogeneous higher-dimensional problem remains unclassified; the final quadratic-term objection was operator-adjudicated as a double-counted summand rather than a mathematical defect.
tldr: Can lower-rank observations sharpen top-rank creative-effect estimates when rank discounts are unknown but shared across advertisers, and how should advertisers be allocated to ranks? This note proves a local design theory for real-valued parallel experiments: a rank-specific positive-semidefinite nuisance-elimination decomposition, strict coordinatewise pooling gains, an exact if-and-only-if frontier for balanced minimax allocation, a floor-clipped radical solution for arbitrary two-advertiser heterogeneity, and primal/dual assignment certificates. Two crossing higher-dimensional orbit reductions are exact: arbitrary signed lift heterogeneity reduces to an explicit rank-one convex program when lower-rank discount magnitudes coincide, while arbitrary admissible lower-rank discounts reduce to an \((A-1)\)-dimensional convex program when one advertiser has a distinct lift magnitude and the others share one magnitude. Their intersection is the certified scalar one-outlier theorem. A generic arbitrary-lift plus unequal-discount classification and finite-sample or adaptive WLS inference remain outside the proved scope.
gap: The closest causal experiment treats rank discounts as known in its principal information benchmark and shows a negative result only for a naive separately calibrated split estimator when discounts are unknown. Position-bias papers learn shared multiplicative factors for ranking or propensity goals, and optimal-design papers supply generic conic machinery, but the inspected sources do not characterize the causal lift information left after shared discount nuisance removal or the resulting Birkhoff-constrained minimax allocation.
fill: Prove the common-null-space Schur decomposition and strict pooling theorem, then use that geometry to establish the balanced-design iff frontier, the exact two-advertiser formula with all edge cases, and a rank-specific assignment certificate and gap for \(A\ge3\).
